JRLC 3600.finalExam: Counts as an assessment, so course notes and readings are allowed and AI is not.
JRLC 3600.attendance: Attendance is required and collected as participation through Top Hat, usually with a question during class and sometimes with the attendance function.
JRLC 3600.lateWork: Late written work is accepted with a 10% deduction from the assessed grade for each 24-hour period or part of one past the due date; assessment and quiz deadlines are final, so no late submissions for
other: AI may not be used on any assessment, and no assignment or discussion post may be generated by an AI tool; either counts as unauthorized assistance.
AI tools may be used only to support your own thinking (exploring news topics, organizing notes, brainstorming), and anything they produce must be fact-checked.
Submissions are checked with Turnitin for plagiarism and AI; a score of 20% or higher gets a careful review, and suspected violations go to the Office of Academ

objectives: Students will identify and understand the typology of misinformation, disinformation, and malinformation.
Students will identify concepts like filter bubble, homophily, confirmation bias, echo chambers, as well as bots, trolls, and sock puppets on various digital platforms.
Students will use tools to practice digital fact-checking.
Students will employ a codified digital verification process for news and digital journalistic content.
Students will understand how journalists work by fact-checking journalistic stories and reflecting on effectiveness of the effort.
Students will participate in a newsroom simulation to employ conceptual knowledge and tools gained from course.

objectives: Students will make better pictures -- whether for a media outlet, personal use, or a client.
They will assess and apply technical, compositional, and storytelling methods.
Students will determine quality storytelling methods to tell a coherent and compelling narrative through their photo(s).
Students will examine how photography can serve a greater purpose to themselves and to the world.
Students will evaluate the various career paths they can take in photography and how photography can enhance other careers.

Students will develop the skills needed to produce or supervise production of relevant fundraising materials.
